Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0024-reverse-97", "row_sha256": "ad1cc4dd21dbd95b3c21a7a2c15ae621cdc382a52bd982d424535c3470668593", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you make this into a useful volunteer event plan brief? the event is the Harbor Lane Shared Garden workday, on saturday june 14, from 9 in the morning until 1. the address is 18 Harbor Lane, North Quay. the main idea is to get a few seasonal jobs done with the people who signed up, and make the plan practical for the coordinators to use on the day. please include a timed run of day, ways to split people into work groups, what needs to be set up, the supplies, safety and access details, refreshments, and closing tasks. don't write the event plan itself in this reply; i need a clearer prompt that i can hand over for that work.

there are some notes from the coordinators below, please include them rather than just giving a general description. Mara is handling the site, Luis is coordinating tools and the work areas, Nina has registration, and Owen is arranging refreshments. the draft should be addressed to Leonie, not Ellis. Leonie is the garden liaison who asked for a planning document; make the recipient wording unambiguous. the event starts at 9, but Mara says volunteers can begin arriving earlier, so distinguish that from the public start time.

Mara's message from the site walk was: “the main garden gate will be open at 8:00, and the meeting room in the adjacent hall will be available from 8:15. the toilets are in that hall. there’s a water tap behind the shed. please keep the fire lane clear all morning, and leave the east bed alone because bulbs are still growing there. no indoor shoes in the hall, please.” the garden and hall are both at 18 Harbor Lane. Mara also said the gate is the normal entrance and there isn't another entrance listed in the notes. include the actual access information, not an invented gate code or another door. the early access times should give the coordinators a chance to set up, not move the advertised start earlier.

Luis sent this after checking the tool area: “we have 8 trowels, 6 hand forks, 4 spades, 2 wheelbarrows and one hose. for the planter job there are 4 unopened cans of outdoor teal paint, 6 brushes and 2 rollers. please count what we have in the plan, and don’t assume there are ladders.” the work being considered is weeding the raised beds, repainting 3 planters, and assembling 2 flat-pack benches. the bench boxes are expected at the hall on friday, but nobody has confirmed that they arrived yet. make the prompt ask the planner to show how these activities could be divided up without treating the delivery as confirmed.

Nina's registration update says there are 24 volunteers on the list: 18 adults, 4 teenagers aged 14 to 17, and 2 children under 12, each attending with an accompanying adult. Five people are coming to this garden for the first time. those are the numbers to use. i don't have a list of volunteer names or preferred jobs. the plan should help the coordinators welcome people and explain the work, but should not assign named individuals to tasks. please keep the age and accompaniment details visible where group arrangements are discussed, rather than describing all 24 people as interchangeable.

Owen's note about food and room setup was: “I can bring tea, water, fruit and rolls. We have two folding tables and 25 chairs. The hall can be used for the welcome and refreshments; please leave it tidy at the end.” include that as the available refreshment and furniture information. don't turn it into a confirmed catered lunch or add food that isn't listed. the event finishes at 1, so the timed schedule needs to allow for packing away and leaving the hall tidy by then. the water tap is also available on site, as Mara noted.

for the plan request, ask for a schedule that covers coordinator setup, volunteer arrival and welcome, a short safety and task briefing, work time, a refreshment pause, and cleanup before the 1 p.m. finish. make clear that 8:00 gate access and 8:15 hall access are setup times, while the workday is advertised as 9:00–1:00. group suggestions should reflect the actual tool quantities and the three proposed jobs. don't claim a job can proceed with equipment that isn't listed; where a practical detail is not known, leave it open for the planner instead of settling it in the brief.

there is also a weather note from Mara: “if heavy rain is forecast, we’ll decide by friday at 4 p.m. whether to postpone. the covered courtyard can be used if it’s only a shower.” include both parts as written, and don't invent a replacement date. the notes don't say who will contact volunteers if the decision changes, so that should remain an open point rather than being assigned to someone. the east bed restriction still applies to the garden work, and the fire lane must stay clear regardless of the weather arrangement.

please organize the eventual plan request into useful sections, with a numbered section if that fits naturally, and ask for a clear, practical document rather than promotional copy. keep the source messages with their speaker names and preserve their quoted details. the last part should include one additional practical source detail: a local plant donor is expected to drop off two trays of seedlings at the garden gate between 8:30 and 8:45 on the day. no one has said what varieties they are or which bed they are for, so don't specify either. that arrival is before the 9 a.m. start and should be included as a coordination detail, not turned into a new volunteer activity.", "output": "Create a practical, clear volunteer event plan for the Harbor Lane Shared Garden workday. Address the planning document to **Leonie, not Ellis**. The event is scheduled for Saturday, June 14, from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at 18 Harbor Lane, North Quay. The plan is for coordinators to use on the day, not promotional copy.

Include a timed schedule, suggested work groups, setup needs, available supplies, access and safety details, refreshments, and closing tasks. Cover coordinator setup, volunteer arrival and welcome, a short safety and task briefing, work time, a refreshment pause, and cleanup before the 1:00 p.m. finish. Distinguish the advertised 9:00 a.m. start from the earlier access times provided for setup.

### 1. Site access and conditions

Mara is handling the site. Her message from the site walk was: “the main garden gate will be open at 8:00, and the meeting room in the adjacent hall will be available from 8:15. the toilets are in that hall. there’s a water tap behind the shed. please keep the fire lane clear all morning, and leave the east bed alone because bulbs are still growing there. no indoor shoes in the hall, please.” Both the garden and hall are at 18 Harbor Lane. The main garden gate is the normal entrance; no other entrance or gate code is listed. Use the 8:00 gate access and 8:15 hall access as setup times, not as an earlier advertised start.

Mara also said: “if heavy rain is forecast, we’ll decide by friday at 4 p.m. whether to postpone. the covered courtyard can be used if it’s only a shower.” Include both parts without inventing a replacement date. The notes do not identify who would contact volunteers if the decision changes, so leave that point open. Keep the east bed restriction and the requirement to keep the fire lane clear in the plan.

### 2. Volunteers and proposed work

Nina’s registration update lists 24 volunteers: 18 adults, 4 teenagers aged 14 to 17, and 2 children under 12, each attending with an accompanying adult. Five people are coming to this garden for the first time. Use those numbers. No list of names or preferred jobs is available, so suggest ways to welcome participants and divide the work without assigning tasks to named individuals. Keep the age and accompaniment details visible when discussing group arrangements.

The proposed work is weeding the raised beds, repainting 3 planters, and assembling 2 flat-pack benches. Luis coordinates tools and work areas. His tool-area message was: “we have 8 trowels, 6 hand forks, 4 spades, 2 wheelbarrows and one hose. for the planter job there are 4 unopened cans of outdoor teal paint, 6 brushes and 2 rollers. please count what we have in the plan, and don’t assume there are ladders.” The bench boxes are expected at the hall on Friday, but their arrival has not been confirmed. Suggest how the activities could be divided without treating the bench delivery as confirmed. Reflect the listed tool quantities, and do not rely on equipment that is not listed. Leave unknown practical details open rather than settling them in the brief.

### 3. Refreshments, room, and other arrivals

Owen is arranging refreshments. His note was: “I can bring tea, water, fruit and rolls. We have two folding tables and 25 chairs. The hall can be used for the welcome and refreshments; please leave it tidy at the end.” Treat these as the available refreshments and furniture. Do not describe them as a confirmed catered lunch or add unlisted food. Include the site water tap noted by Mara and allow time to leave the hall tidy by the 1:00 p.m. finish.

A local plant donor is expected to drop off two trays of seedlings at the garden gate between 8:30 and 8:45 on the day. Include this as a coordination detail before the 9:00 a.m. start, not as a new volunteer activity. The varieties and intended bed are not known; do not specify either.

Keep the source messages with their speaker names and quoted details. Organize the plan request into useful sections, using a numbered section where it fits naturally, and make the resulting document practical for the coordinators to use."}]
